descricao_original: As in mitosis, the nuclear envelope reforms during telophase. The resultant nuclei contain one replicated chromosome of each homologous pair; sister chromatids remain attached. This separation of a homologous pair reduces the number of chromosomes in daughter cells from 2N (diploid) to 1N (haploid). Therefore, meiosis I is called the reductional division.

marcadores.explicacao_original: The cleavage furrow, marking the eventual separation site of the daughter cells, is formed by a contractile ring composed of actin and myosin filaments. Interaction between the filaments tightens the ring and eventually pinches the cell into two daughter cells.
